claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Severe plastic deformation can overcome the alloy's limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness.
Severe plastic deformation will retain or increase the alloy's strength.
Grain refinement through severe plastic deformation will introduce a ductile phase.
The intervention is high-pressure torsion for five rotations at room temperature.
High-pressure torsion will produce a refined grain structure.
High-pressure torsion and grain refinement will reduce internal boundaries.
Grain refinement will reduce dislocation pile-ups.
Reduced dislocation pile-ups will reduce local stress concentrations.
Reduced dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations will enhance tensile ductility.
The treatment will increase elongation at break from 5% to 6.25%, a relative increase of 25%.
The treatment will increase yield strength from 1000 MPa to 1100 MPa, a relative increase of 10%.
The predicted performance applies to tensile testing at room temperature and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says that grain refinement introduces a ductile phase, but the stated structural mediator identifies only grain refinement and reduced internal boundaries, with no new phase or phase-transformation pathway specified.

The proposed grain-refinement treatment is said to reduce internal boundaries. Grain refinement ordinarily implies smaller grains and therefore greater grain-boundary density or area, so the claimed mediator is internally incoherent unless 'internal boundaries' is narrowly defined as lamellar or colony boundaries and their elimination is demonstrated.
